title: Al-Biruni
summary: Born in 973 at Kath in Khwarazm, al-Biruni was taken to Ghazna in 1017 and served at the court of Mahmud of Ghazna, which became his home base. There he studied Indian science and wrote his book on India, completed in 1030, and an astronomical canon with a table of coordinates for about six hundred places. He died at Ghazna in 1048.

uncertainty.note: Birth and death dates are given by the MacTutor biography; EBSCO gives no birth or death date.

where.modern_name: Ghazni, Afghanistan (pinned to Ghazna, where he spent the rest of his life and wrote his India; he was born at Kath, Khwarazm, now Uzbekistan)
where.historical_name: Ghazna, seat of Mahmud of Ghazna (r. 997-1030) per EBSCO

importance.justification: MacTutor credits him with a triangulated estimate of the Earth radius and a table of coordinates for about six hundred places, and lists about 146 works.

sources.title: Al-Biruni (MacTutor biography)
sources.publisher: MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews

reviewer_note: MacTutor gives the birthplace as Kath, Khwarazm and death at Ghazna; EBSCO places the birth in an outlying neighborhood of Khiva. Pin is Ghazna, a city centroid.
